comments.body:
What is this doing exactly? Anytime I see negative numbers in the IR it is suspect to me.

```
 %int-2_1836 = torch.constant.int -2
    %int-1_1837 = torch.constant.int -1
    %1662 = torch.aten.transpose.int %54, %int-2_1836, %int-1_1837 : !torch.vtensor<[128256,16384],f16>, !torch.int, !torch.int -> !torch.vtensor<[16384,128256],f16>
```
From what I can tell, it is trying to transpose the second-to-last dimension (-2 in Python) with the last dimension (-1 in Python).
anyway, lowering to Linalg looks fine.
cc @nirvedhmeshram  I am trying to repro as well... Want to verify if there is non-determinism due to IREE generated code.

@aviator19941  is this supposed to be non-deterministic? 

When I ran on mi355 I get

```
$ python compare_results.py
MATMUL #1: False
MATMUL #2: False
MATMUL #3: False
MATMUL #4: False
```

i.e. fails all the time.
@aviator19941  can you try if you have both arguments come in as input if this gives the right results?

Ok, modified the test to 
```
module @module {                                                                                                                                                                                                  func.func @mm_repro(%arg0: !torch.vtensor<[?,16384],f16>, %arg1 : !torch.vtensor<[128256, 16384], f16>) -> !torch.vtensor<[?,128256],f16> attributes {torch.assume_strict_symbolic_shapes} {
    %73 = torch.symbolic_int "s1" {min_val = 2, max_val = 4095} : !torch.int
    %int-2_1836 = torch.constant.int -2
    %int-1_1837 = torch.constant.int -1
    %1662 = torch.aten.transpose.int %arg1, %int-2_1836, %int-1_1837 : !torch.vtensor<[128256,16384],f16>, !torch.int, !torch.int -> !torch.vtensor<[16384,128256],f16>
    %int5_1838 = torch.constant.int 5
    %1663 = torch.prims.convert_element_type %1662, %int5_1838 : !torch.vtensor<[16384,128256],f16>, !torch.int -> !torch.vtensor<[16384,128256],f16>
    %1667 = torch.aten.mm %arg0, %1663 : !torch.vtensor<[?,16384],f16>, !torch.vtensor<[16384,128256],f16> -> !torch.vtensor<[?,128256],f16>
    torch.bind_symbolic_shape %1667, [%73], affine_map<()[s0] -> (s0 * 128, 128256)> : !torch.vtensor<[?,128256],f16>
    return %1667 : !torch.vtensor<[?,128256],f16>
  }
}
```

with this run command

```
iree-run-module \
    --hip_use_streams=true \
    --parameters=model=/shark-dev/llama3.1/405b/instruct/weights/fp4/fp4_2025_07_10_fn.irpa \
    --module=fp4_2.vmfb \
    --device=hip://0 \
    --function=mm_repro \
    --input=@repro_input.npy \
    --input=@weight.npy \
    --output=@repro_output_1.npy
```

with `repro_input.npy` same as above and `weight.npy` created by 

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> weight = np.random.rand(128256, 16384).astype('float16')
>>> np.save("weight.npy", weight)
```

Running the command many times produces different result everytime.

Also these tensors are greater than 2GB. Hope it isnt some 32-bit indexing issue.

I took an initial look at the pipeline this is going through and it is `LLVMGPUVectorDistribute` with the following matmul and lowering config
```
ins(%12, %13 : tensor<?x16384xf16>, tensor<128256x16384xf16>) outs(%16 : tensor<?x128256xf32>) 
attrs =  {lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{lane_basis = [[1, 1, 64], [0, 1, 2]], 
partial_reduction = [0, 0, 4096], subgroup_basis = [[1, 1, 16], [0, 1, 2]], 
thread = [0, 0, 4], workgroup = [1, 1, 0]}>
```
I am not that familiar with this pipeline so perhaps @Groverkss will have to take a look at it. 
Is it expected that `BlockDynamicDimensionsPass` didnt do anything for this dispatch, @MaheshRavishankar ?

Updating with the root cause. Seems like we were launching too many workgroups along x-dimension and that was causing the kernel to silently fail. Adding `--iree-llvmgpu-set-workgroup-distribution-along=z` fixes the issue. I will fix the issue either later this week or next week.

The issue is fixed on this branch: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/tree/shared/fixMaxNumWorkgroups

It isn't quite in a landable state yet IMO, since we are relying on the GPU target attr, but it should work if you want to cherry-pick.

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/21584 Fixes this issue, but really this is not non-determinism. This was a kernel launch failure silently missed.

@AWoloszyn  do you have cycles to look into this. It is being fixed on main, but if you go to a point before my fix you should be able to see the failure not stopping the execution. Is that expected? Is there something the caller needs to do to catch these errors?

If we fail to launch a kernel we pass an error back up through the semaphore, which should be caught on any host wait. Somewhat curious what is going on. I can take a look to see if we are failing to propagate an error up. But we have seen this properly report errors before so not sure what's up here.

issue.body:
### What happened?

We are seeing non-deterministic results in Llama 405b when exporting 4 or more attention layers. It seems like there is an issue loading the weights properly since the left hand side of the `torch.aten.mm` is constant over multiple runs, but the right hand side - which is derived from the `output.weight` weight tensor - cannot be saved to numpy via `iree-run-module`. The output of the `torch.aten.mm` is always non-deterministic, so it leads me to believe the issue has to do with loading the weight tensors. I have a small repro [here](https://gist.github.com/aviator19941/eadef1c8d4c2748f6edc8107fa6f4cda) with repro instructions below.

### Steps to reproduce your issue

1. Login to the `smci355-ccs-aus-n10-09` machine which uses rocm 7.0.
2. Download repro.mlir: 
```
wget https://gist.githubusercontent.com/aviator19941/eadef1c8d4c2748f6edc8107fa6f4cda/raw/d90b978bfd60f8d1271f60f344a87c63efaf7892/repro.mlir
```
3. Download compile, run, and compare scripts and input:
```
wget https://gist.githubusercontent.com/aviator19941/c72ade6f44d6f10c0efaec7740f8bbf4/raw/2e25e4cea36a13148e2f5e7ed3a626d3865eaf37/compile.sh
wget https://gist.githubusercontent.com/aviator19941/7420935f6868353eae3f5ad00af68234/raw/e04b42caccbd602f4d37eec5dccc5fe6f1e948c0/run_repro.sh
wget https://gist.githubusercontent.com/aviator19941/4d0c7b5a8964f3d7a0e74cf9d93cddff/raw/74a503a03e0b5657dd1d1fd18b9623546ed36cdc/compare_results.py
wget https://sharkpublic.blob.core.windows.net/sharkpublic/halo-models/llm-dev/llama3_405b/repro_input.npy
```
4. Set up venv:
```
python3.11 -m venv .test
source .test/bin/activate
pip install -f https://iree.dev/pip-release-links.html --upgrade --pre \
  iree-base-compiler iree-base-runtime
```
5. Run scripts:
```
./compile.sh && ./run_repro.sh && python compare_results.py
```


### What component(s) does this issue relate to?

_No response_

### Version information

iree-base-compiler 3.7.0rc20250725
iree-base-runtime  3.7.0rc20250725

### Additional context

_No response_
issue.title: Non-deterministic results after loading Llama 405b weight
